title: From the regional lessons to a human GeoClick round
voicePerspective: Third person; he is the human player
premise: The user states that the player watched the regional lessons and learned from them. Spoken claims follow the visible actions and final result in third person.

observedResult.scope: 48 contiguous states plus District of Columbia; Alaska and Hawaii absent

presentation.notes: Crop desktop/recording chrome; retain game and tray; reserve top band for optional captions. Resample the variable-rate source to 30 fps without changing its timeline. Original source audio measures -91 dB and is silent.

cues.text: He hides the redundant interface with the eye controls, making more room for the map.
After watching the regional lessons, he now tests what he remembers. He starts placing names without the lesson narration guiding each answer.
He takes a name from the tray and places it on its matching region. The green fill confirms a correct answer.
The quiz does not follow the lessons' regional order. As new names enter the tray, he moves between different parts of the country.
Arizona, New Mexico and Indiana are already green. Those completed outlines remain visible as he continues with the next names.
He zooms into the central and eastern states. Larger outlines give him more room to make accurate placements.
Each successful placement leaves its name on the map. The tray refills, so he still has to identify the locations of the remaining names.
He pans to keep the relevant area in view, then continues placing names. The recording shows a steady sequence of green answers.
The growing green map connects the regions from the videos. He moves from one part of the country to another as the tray changes.
Completed states provide visible reference points. Their neighbouring outlines remain available as he works through the still-unlabelled regions.
He keeps adjusting the map's position and scale. The same geography can be viewed as a whole country or as a smaller cluster of states.
The northeast now contains several completed labels. He continues switching between nearby targets and names from farther across the map.
California's long coastal outline is now filled in. The large western shapes and the smaller eastern shapes belong to the same recall task.
Across the South, the green regions are joining up. He continues placing names while the completed states stay labelled around them.
He broadens the view again to reach other regions. The map is increasingly green, but several unplaced names are still waiting in the tray.
He maintains the same routine: choose a name, locate its region, place it, and continue after the green confirmation.
Here he brings the northeast closer. Small targets such as Delaware and the District of Columbia need more screen space than the big western states.
He moves back across the country as more names become available. The remaining tray, rather than a fixed regional route, determines the next location.
This quiz contains the forty-eight contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Alaska and Hawaii are outside this particular map.
Each clean answer is progress. In GeoClick, the full Known label is earned across repeated successful rounds; this recording shows a first-pass performance.
The remaining eastern targets need precision. He zooms in again, giving the small borders more space for accurate placement.
He places the District of Columbia in the small area around Washington. The completed eastern targets now carry their green labels.
He returns to the western interior for the last names, ending with Colorado. The final placement completes the green map.
Forty-nine out of forty-nine, correct on the first try. Zero mistakes. He has put the regional lessons into practice.
